name: Blue Moon Mark 1
short_status: In development, waiting on its rocket: pathfinder Endurance is fully assembled and thermal-vacuum tested, with a cryogenic propellant-loading test next, but the May 28, 2026 New Glenn pad explosion pushed its debut to early 2027 (NASA and Blue Origin, Sep 15, 2026); VIPER rides a second MK1, targeted for 2027 (NASA, Oct 20, 2026).
tagline: Blue Origin · United States · Programme · 2027 · Commercial and multipolar In development
stats: cargo MK1 is rated to deliver to the lunar surface
NASA task order to land VIPER on the second MK1
precision-landing accuracy the pathfinder must prove
MK1 flights so far; NASA's launch schedule lists the debut for 2027 (as of Nov 2026)

facts.label: Status (as of Nov 2, 2026)
facts.value: Pathfinder lander Endurance fully assembled and environmental-tested, with cryogenic propellant loading the next test before integration for launch (NASA, 4 Aug 2026), but grounded with its rocket after the New Glenn pad explosion; first flight in the first part of 2027 per NASA's Moon Base program manager and early 2027 per Blue Origin's senior director of civil space (both 15 Sep 2026). NASA's launch schedule lists 2027 with no month (updated 21 Oct 2026)

facts.label: Lander
facts.value: 8.05 m tall, 3.08 m diameter, 21,350 kg fueled; up to 3,000 kg of cargo to the lunar surface on a single New Glenn launch

facts.label: Engine
facts.value: One BE-7: dual-expander liquid oxygen/liquid hydrogen, up to 44 kN, throttling down to 8.9 kN for landing

facts.label: NASA payloads (CLPS delivery CT-3)
facts.value: SCALPSS 1.x stereo cameras (plume-surface imaging during descent) and a Laser Retroreflector Array, bound for the lunar south pole

facts.label: CLPS task order value
facts.value: About $6.1 million (August 2024) to fly SCALPSS; small because Blue Origin funds the pathfinder mission itself as a demonstration

facts.label: Name
facts.value: First MK1 lander named Endurance on 20 January 2026, for Ernest Shackleton's ship, as it shipped to Houston for testing

facts.label: Landing target
facts.value: Shackleton Connecting Ridge, lunar south pole; NASA designated the flight Moon Base I at its 26 May 2026 Moon Base announcement

facts.label: Environmental testing
facts.value: Completed in Thermal Vacuum Chamber A at NASA's Johnson Space Center, announced 4 May 2026

facts.label: VIPER assignment
facts.value: NASA release 25-064 (19 September 2025): task order worth up to $190 million to deliver the VIPER rover on a second MK1, targeted late 2027; delivery option exercised only after review of the base task and the first MK1 flight

facts.label: VIPER backstory
facts.value: Canceled by NASA on 17 July 2024 on cost and schedule grounds after about $450 million spent, with the nearly finished rover kept intact; revived via the Blue Origin award

facts.label: New Glenn record (as of Nov 2026)
facts.value: Three flights: orbit on the 16 January 2025 debut; first booster landing with ESCAPADE on 13 November 2025; booster reflight 19 April 2026 that left its payload in a wrong orbit

facts.label: Pad explosion
facts.value: 28 May 2026: the next New Glenn, slated to carry Amazon Leo satellites, was destroyed during a static-fire test at Launch Complex 36, with extensive pad damage and no injuries

facts.label: Return to flight
facts.value: Blue Origin aims to fly New Glenn again before the end of 2026 (per CEO Dave Limp, 30 June 2026), shifting to hybrid vertical integration after losing its transporter-erector; NASA says its lunar plans can tolerate a slip into 2027. In October 2026 Jeff Bezos said the company was still pushing to fly again before the end of the year, while its LC-36A pad was being rebuilt (Spaceflight Now, 16 Oct 2026). On 28 Oct 2026 SpaceNews reported that Blue Origin expects the rebuilt pad to be ready by the first half of December to support a return to flight in 2026

timeline: Jeff Bezos unveils the Blue Moon lander program in Washington, DC
NASA announces cancellation of the VIPER rover after about $450 million spent; the finished rover is preserved
Aug 2024
NASA awards Blue Origin CLPS task order CT-3, about $6.1 million, to fly SCALPSS on the MK1 pathfinder
New Glenn reaches orbit on its first flight; the booster is lost during its landing attempt
NASA assigns VIPER to a second Blue Moon MK1: task order worth up to $190 million, delivery targeted late 2027
New Glenn's second flight launches NASA's ESCAPADE Mars probes and lands its booster at sea for the first time
Blue Origin names the first MK1 lander Endurance and debuts its mission patch as the lander ships to Houston
New Glenn's third flight reuses the recovered booster and lands it again, but an upper-stage malfunction strands the BlueBird 7 satellite in an unusable orbit
NASA announces Endurance completed environmental testing in Johnson Space Center's Thermal Vacuum Chamber A
NASA's Moon Base announcement brands the pathfinder flight Moon Base I and adds MK1 cargo delivery task orders ($188 million plus a $280.4 million option period)
The next New Glenn is destroyed in a static-fire explosion at Launch Complex 36, heavily damaging the pad; no injuries
At NASA's Moon Base event, Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp outlines New Glenn return-to-flight plans and points the MK1 pathfinder to early 2027
Targeted early 2027
Pathfinder launch, listed for 2027 on NASA's launch schedule (as of Nov 2026) and early 2027 by Blue Origin, pending New Glenn return to flight and pad recovery
Targeted 2027

VIPER delivery, 2027 per NASA's October 20, 2026 update (late 2027 at the September 2025 award), contingent on NASA exercising the option after the first MK1 flight; NASA says the fully built rover is in final testing at Johnson Space Center
